Table customer.segment {
  segment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the customer segmentation classification record.']
  party_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer party being segmented. Links to the customer master record.']
  ami_deployment_cohort varchar [note: 'AMI smart meter deployment wave or cohort identifier indicating when the customer received AMI meter installation. Used for AMI deployment tracking, interval data availability determination, and time-of-use rate migration planning. Examples: WAVE-1-2018, WAVE-2-2019, LEGACY-AMR (not yet upgraded to AMI).']
  annual_consumption_kwh decimal(15,2) [note: 'Trailing twelve-month total electric energy consumption in kilowatt-hours at the time of segment assignment. Used for load profile group classification, customer value tier determination, and rate case cost-of-service allocation. Nullable for new customers without consumption history.']
  assignment_reason varchar [note: 'The business reason or trigger for this segment classification assignment. Initial enrollment occurs at customer onboarding. Rate change reflects tariff modification. Program enrollment occurs when customer joins income assistance or DER program. Annual review reflects periodic re-certification. Customer request reflects customer-initiated rate or program change. System migration reflects data conversion. Regulatory mandate reflects PUC-ordered reclassification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: initial_enrollment|rate_change|program_enrollment|annual_review|customer_request|system_migration|regulatory_mandate — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  assignment_source varchar [note: 'The system or process that originated this segment classification. CIS system assignments come from Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U customer master. CRM system assignments come from Salesforce campaign or program enrollment. Manual override reflects analyst or customer service representative adjustment. Third party verification reflects income verification service for CARE/FERA. Regulatory filing reflects PUC rate case assignment. AMI analytics reflects MDMS load profile analysis.']
  battery_storage_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has an interconnected battery energy storage system. True if customer has active battery storage interconnection agreement. Used for demand response program eligibility, grid services procurement, and DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System) enrollment.']
  cpp_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer is eligible for Critical Peak Pricing program enrollment. True if customer meets minimum demand threshold and has AMI meter with interval data capability. CPP programs charge higher rates during system peak events (typically 10-15 days per year) to incentivize load reduction.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this segment classification record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  customer_value_tier varchar [note: 'Customer lifetime value segmentation tier for retention and engagement strategies. High-value customers have high consumption, low payment risk, and long tenure. Medium-value customers have moderate consumption and stable payment history. Low-value customers have low consumption or short tenure. At-risk customers show indicators of potential churn or payment default.']
  demand_response_tier varchar [note: 'Demand response program eligibility tier based on load flexibility, historical participation, and curtailment capability. Tier 1 customers have high curtailment capability (>50 kW) and reliable participation history. Tier 2 customers have moderate capability (10-50 kW). Tier 3 customers have low capability (<10 kW) or are residential participants. Not eligible customers do not meet minimum requirements for DR program participation.']
  der_adoption_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has adopted any Distributed Energy Resource (DER) technology including solar photovoltaic, battery energy storage, electric vehicle, or combined heat and power (CHP). True if customer has one or more DER assets interconnected or registered. Used for DER program targeting, grid planning, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance reporting.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date when this segment classification becomes effective and active for the customer. Used for historical trend analysis, rate case cost-of-service studies, and program eligibility determination. Segment assignments are versioned to support point-in-time queries.']
  ev_owner_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer owns or leases an electric vehicle and is enrolled in an EV-specific rate or program. True if customer has registered EV ownership or is on EV time-of-use rate. Used for EV program targeting, managed charging programs, and transportation electrification planning.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'The date when this segment classification expires or is superseded by a new assignment. Nullable for currently active segments with no planned expiration. Used for historical trend analysis and regulatory rate case testimony showing customer migration between segments over time.']
  income_tier varchar [note: 'Income-based program eligibility tier for low-income assistance programs. CARE (California Alternate Rates for Energy) provides 30-35% discount for households at or below 200% of federal poverty level. FERA (Family Electric Rate Assistance) provides 18% discount for households between 200-250% of federal poverty level. Medical baseline provides additional allowance for customers with qualifying medical equipment. Standard tier receives no income-based discount.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this segment classification record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and incremental data processing.']
  life_support_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has registered life-support or medical baseline equipment that requires continuous electric service. True if customer has active medical baseline certification. Used for outage prioritization, planned outage notification requirements, and medical baseline rate allowance application.']
  load_factor decimal(5,4) [note: 'Ratio of average load to peak load over the trailing twelve months, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. High load factor (>0.7) indicates consistent baseload consumption typical of industrial customers. Low load factor (<0.4) indicates peaky consumption typical of commercial customers. Used for load profile group classification and rate design analysis.']
  load_profile_group varchar [note: 'Load profile classification grouping customers by consumption pattern for load forecasting and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) projections. Examples: RES-STANDARD (standard residential), RES-HIGH-USE (high-consumption residential), COMM-RETAIL (retail commercial), COMM-OFFICE (office commercial), IND-CONTINUOUS (24/7 industrial), IND-SHIFT (shift-based industrial).']
  peak_demand_kw decimal(12,2) [note: 'Maximum 15-minute interval demand in kilowatts during the trailing twelve months at the time of segment assignment. Used for rate class determination (small vs large commercial threshold), demand response tier assignment, and capacity cost allocation. Nullable for residential customers without demand metering.']
  priority varchar [note: 'Numeric priority ranking when a customer has multiple concurrent segment classifications. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used to determine which segment takes precedence for rate application when multiple segments conflict. For example, CARE income tier (priority 1) overrides standard rate class (priority 5) for billing purposes.']
  program_enrollment_date date [note: 'The date when the customer enrolled in the program or rate associated with this segment classification. Applicable for income assistance programs (CARE, FERA), demand response programs, time-of-use rates, and DER programs. Nullable for non-program segments such as standard rate class assignments.']
  rate_class varchar [note: 'Primary rate class classification for tariff application and cost-of-service allocation. Residential serves single-family and multi-family dwellings. Small commercial serves businesses under demand threshold (typically <50 kW). Large commercial serves businesses above demand threshold. Industrial serves manufacturing and heavy industry. Agricultural serves farms and irrigation. Street lighting serves municipal and private lighting.']
  recertification_due_date date [note: 'The date by which the customer must recertify eligibility for this segment classification. Required for income-based programs (CARE, FERA) which mandate annual or biennial recertification. Nullable for segments that do not require periodic recertification.']
  segment_code varchar [note: 'The specific segment classification code assigned to this party or account within the segment type. Examples: RES (residential), COMM-SM (small commercial), IND-LG (large industrial), CARE (California Alternate Rates for Energy), FERA (Family Electric Rate Assistance), SOLAR-NEM (Net Energy Metering solar customer), EV-OWNER (electric vehicle owner), DR-TIER1 (demand response tier 1 eligible).']
  segment_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the segment classification criteria, business rules for assignment, and intended use cases. Supports regulatory rate case testimony and program design documentation.']
  segment_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the segment classification for reporting and analytics. Examples: Residential Customer, Small Commercial, Large Industrial, CARE-Eligible Low Income, High-Value Customer, Solar NEM Customer, EV Owner, Demand Response Participant.']
  segment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this segment classification record. Active segments are currently in effect. Pending segments are scheduled for future effective date. Expired segments have passed their expiration date. Superseded segments have been replaced by a newer assignment. Cancelled segments were voided before becoming effective.']
  segment_type varchar [note: 'The dimension or category of segmentation being applied. Rate class segments customers by tariff eligibility (residential, commercial, industrial). Load profile groups customers by consumption pattern. Income tier identifies program eligibility (CARE, FERA). Customer value tiers support retention strategies. DER adoption flags solar, battery, EV ownership. Demand response eligibility determines DR program participation.']
  solar_customer_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has an interconnected solar photovoltaic system under Net Energy Metering (NEM) or other solar tariff. True if customer has active solar interconnection agreement. Used for NEM billing, RPS compliance tracking, and distributed generation forecasting.']
  tou_rate_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer is eligible for time-of-use rate enrollment based on AMI meter availability and rate class. True if customer has AMI meter and rate class supports TOU tariff. Used for TOU rate migration campaigns and dynamic pricing program targeting.']

  Note: 'Customer segmentation classification record assigning a party or account to one or more business-defined segments for targeting, rate design analysis, and program eligibility determination. Segment dimensions include rate class (residential, small commercial, large commercial, industrial), load profile group, income tier (CARE-eligible, FERA-eligible, standard), customer value tier, DER adoption flags (solar, battery storage, EV), demand response eligibility tier, AMI smart meter deployment cohort, and life-support/medical baseline flag. Segment assignments are versioned with effective and expiration dates to support historical trend analysis and regulatory rate case testimony. Used by regulatory affairs for rate case cost-of-service studies, by DSM teams for program targeting, and by load forecasting for IRP class-level projections.'

Table customer.account_hierarchy {
  account_hierarchy_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the account hierarchy relationship record. Primary key for the account hierarchy entity.']
  child_account_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the child account in the hierarchy. Represents the subordinate account whose billing and usage data may be aggregated to the parent account. Used for multi-site enterprises, individual units in master-metered buildings, and departmental accounts within large commercial and industrial (C&I) customers.']
  parent_account_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the parent account in the hierarchy. For consolidated billing structures, this represents the master account that aggregates billing and usage from child accounts. Used in corporate umbrella structures, property management companies, and master-metered multi-dwelling unit (MDU) complexes.']
  allocation_method varchar [note: 'Method used to allocate charges or usage from parent to child accounts in master-metered or shared service scenarios. Proportional allocates based on square footage or unit count. Fixed percentage uses predefined allocation percentages. Equal split divides evenly among child accounts. Custom uses business-rule-driven allocation logic. None indicates no allocation is performed. Common in multi-dwelling unit (MDU) complexes and shared facility arrangements.']
  allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Fixed percentage used to allocate charges or usage from parent to child account when allocation method is fixed percentage. Value between 0.00 and 100.00. Sum of allocation percentages across all child accounts under a parent should equal 100.00. Used in master-metered multi-dwelling unit (MDU) billing and shared facility cost allocation.']
  billing_aggregation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether billing amounts from the child account are aggregated into the parent account invoice. True enables consolidated billing statements for multi-site enterprises and property management companies. False maintains separate billing while preserving the hierarchical relationship for reporting purposes. Integrates with Oracle CC&B billing engine and Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud for key account management.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the account hierarchy relationship record was first created in the Customer Information System (CIS). Supports audit trail requirements for regulatory compliance and internal controls under Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). Integrates with Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U audit logging.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when the account hierarchy relationship becomes active and billing aggregation or reporting begins. Used for move-in/move-out processing, corporate restructuring, and property management transitions. Supports regulatory reporting requirements for customer-of-record tracking to Public Utility Commission (PUC).']
  end_date date [note: 'Date when the account hierarchy relationship terminates. Null for open-ended relationships. Used for move-out processing, corporate restructuring, property management transitions, and account closure workflows. Supports historical analysis of customer account structures and regulatory reporting to Public Utility Commission (PUC).']
  hierarchy_level varchar [note: 'Numeric depth of the account in the hierarchy tree structure. Level 1 represents the top-level parent account. Each subsequent level increments by 1. Supports multi-tier organizational structures common in large commercial and industrial (C&I) customers with regional, divisional, and site-level accounts.']
  hierarchy_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the account hierarchy relationship. Consolidated billing aggregates multiple accounts into a single invoice. Master-metered applies to multi-dwelling unit (MDU) complexes where a single meter serves multiple units. Corporate umbrella links accounts under a single enterprise entity. Property management groups accounts managed by a property management company. Municipal account represents government entity hierarchies. Franchise represents utility franchise relationships.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the account hierarchy relationship record was most recently updated. Tracks changes to hierarchy type, effective dates, allocation methods, or status transitions. Supports audit trail requirements for regulatory compliance and internal controls under Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX).']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional information about the account hierarchy relationship. May include business justification, special billing instructions, regulatory requirements, or historical context. Used by customer service representatives (CSR) and key account managers for reference during customer interactions and billing dispute resolution.']
  priority_sequence varchar [note: 'Numeric ordering used to determine processing sequence when multiple hierarchy relationships exist for the same account. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used in complex organizational structures where an account may participate in multiple hierarchies (e.g., both a corporate umbrella and a property management relationship). Ensures deterministic billing and reporting behavior.']
  relationship_owner varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the business user or key account manager responsible for managing this account hierarchy relationship. Used for customer relationship management (CRM) workflows in Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud. Supports large commercial and industrial (C&I) account management and enterprise customer service delivery.']
  relationship_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the account hierarchy relationship. Active indicates the relationship is currently in effect and billing aggregation or reporting is operational. Inactive indicates the relationship has been deactivated but not removed. Pending indicates the relationship is awaiting approval or activation. Suspended indicates temporary hold. Terminated indicates the relationship has been permanently ended.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record that originated this account hierarchy relationship. CC&B represents Oracle Customer Care and Billing. IS-U represents SAP Industry Solution for Utilities. CRM represents Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud. MDM represents Master Data Management system. MANUAL represents manually entered relationships. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across enterprise systems.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of this account hierarchy relationship in the source operational system. Used for data lineage tracking, reconciliation, and bidirectional synchronization between the lakehouse and operational systems (Oracle CC&B, SAP IS-U, Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud). Supports troubleshooting and audit trail requirements.']
  usage_aggregation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether energy usage (kilowatt-hour (kWh) or thousand cubic feet (MCF) of gas) from the child account is aggregated into parent account usage reporting. True enables enterprise-level usage analysis for large commercial and industrial (C&I) customers. False maintains separate usage tracking. Supports demand response (DR) program enrollment, energy efficiency (EE) program participation, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance reporting.']

  Note: 'Hierarchical relationship structure linking parent and child accounts for commercial and industrial customers with complex organizational structures — including multi-site enterprises, property management companies, municipal accounts, and master-metered MDU (multi-dwelling unit) complexes. Stores parent account ID, child account ID, hierarchy type (consolidated billing, master-metered, corporate umbrella), hierarchy level, effective date, and end date. Enables consolidated billing statements, enterprise-level usage reporting, and key account management workflows in Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud. Supports large commercial and industrial (C&I) account management and PUC reporting on large customer classes.'
}

Table customer.preference {
  preference_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the customer preference record. Primary key.']
  account_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific customer account this preference applies to. Nullable if preference is set at party level rather than account level.']
  party_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer party who owns this preference. Links to the party master entity.']

  contact_time_window_end varchar [note: 'The latest time of day (HH:MM format, 24-hour clock) the customer is willing to receive non-emergency communications. Used for outbound call scheduling and SMS delivery timing to comply with TCPA restrictions on contact hours.']
  contact_time_window_start varchar [note: 'The earliest time of day (HH:MM format, 24-hour clock) the customer is willing to receive non-emergency communications. Used for outbound call scheduling and SMS delivery timing to comply with TCPA restrictions on contact hours.']
  delivery_channel varchar [note: 'The preferred communication channel through which the customer wishes to receive notifications for this preference category. Supports multi-channel customer engagement strategy.']

  effective_start_date date [note: 'The date from which this preference setting becomes active and should be honored by communication systems. Supports scheduled preference changes and regulatory compliance with opt-out request timing requirements.']
  external_preference_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier for this preference record in the source system (CC&B, Salesforce, SAP IS-U). Supports cross-system reconciliation and bidirectional synchronization.']
  is_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the contact information associated with this preference has been verified through a confirmation process (e.g., double opt-in for email, SMS confirmation code). Critical for TCPA compliance and reducing communication delivery failures.']
  last_modified_by varchar [note: 'The user ID or system identifier that last modified this preference record. Supports audit trail and accountability for preference changes.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this preference record was last updated. Supports change tracking and regulatory compliance audit requirements.']
  mobile_device_token varchar [note: 'The push notification device token for mobile app notifications. Used by mobile notification services (APNS, FCM) to deliver push notifications to the customers registered mobile device.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context or special instructions related to this preference. Supports customer service representatives in understanding unique customer communication requirements.']
  notification_email varchar [note: 'The specific email address to use for this preference category if email is the selected delivery channel. May differ from the primary account email. Supports multi-email management for different communication types.']
  notification_phone varchar [note: 'The specific phone number to use for this preference category if SMS or IVR is the selected delivery channel. May differ from the primary account phone. Supports multi-phone management for different communication types. Format follows E.164 international standard.']
  opt_in_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has opted in or out of receiving communications for this preference category and channel combination. Critical for TCPA and CAN-SPAM compliance.']
  preference_category varchar [note: 'The type of communication or service preference being configured. Defines what kind of notification or communication this preference controls. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: outage_alert|demand_response_notification|planned_outage_notification|billing_statement_ready|payment_confirmation|payment_reminder|marketing_communication|service_appointment_reminder|energy_usage_report|rate_change_notification|program_enrollment_confirmation — promote to reference product]']
  preference_source varchar [note: 'The channel or system through which this preference was originally captured or set. Supports audit trail and preference data lineage tracking.']
  preferred_language varchar [note: 'The language in which the customer prefers to receive communications. Uses 3-letter ISO 639-2 language codes. Supports multilingual customer base and regulatory requirements for language access. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ENG|SPA|FRA|CHI|VIE|KOR|RUS|ARA|POR|GER — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  set_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this preference was originally established by the customer or system. Critical for TCPA and CAN-SPAM compliance audit trails demonstrating when consent was obtained.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this preference record originated. Supports data lineage tracking and multi-system integration reconciliation in hybrid CIS environments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CC&B|Salesforce|SAP_IS-U|Customer_Portal|Mobile_App|Call_Center|Legacy_Migration — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  suppression_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this preference is currently suppressed due to delivery failures, compliance holds, or customer service blocks. When true, communications should not be sent regardless of opt-in status.']
  suppression_reason varchar [note: 'The reason why communications are suppressed for this preference. Supports compliance with do-not-contact regulations and customer service escalation management.']
  suppression_start_date date [note: 'The date from which communication suppression became effective for this preference. Supports time-bound suppression management and audit trail.']
  unsubscribe_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text field capturing the reason provided by the customer when opting out of a communication preference. Supports customer experience analysis and communication strategy improvement.']
  verification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the contact information for this preference was verified. Supports audit trail for double opt-in compliance and contact data quality management.']

  Note: 'Customer communication and service preference record capturing opt-in/opt-out settings and notification channel choices at the party or account level. Stores preference category (outage alert, demand response event notification, planned outage notification, billing statement ready, payment confirmation, payment reminder, marketing communication), preferred delivery channel (email, SMS, push notification, mail, IVR), preferred language, preferred contact time window, and preference effective/expiration dates. Does NOT track program enrollments (see enrollment product) or legally binding consents (see consent product). Sourced from Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud and CC&B notification preferences. Supports TCPA compliance for automated contact channel selection and CAN-SPAM opt-out requirements.'

  rate_structure_type varchar [note: 'Pricing structure methodology: flat (single rate), tiered (increasing block rates), TOU (Time-of-Use with period-based pricing), CPP (Critical Peak Pricing), demand (based on peak kW), real-time pricing (hourly market-based), or net metering (bidirectional energy credit). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: flat|tiered|tou|cpp|demand|real_time_pricing|net_metering — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  seasonal_definition varchar [note: 'JSON or delimited string defining seasonal periods and associated rate adjustments. Example: Summer (June-September): base rate + $0.03/kWh; Winter (October-May): base rate. Nullable if seasonal_variation_flag is False.']
  seasonal_variation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rate schedule has seasonal rate variations (e.g., summer vs. winter rates). True if rates vary by season; False if rates are constant year-round.']
  special_contract_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rate schedule is a special contract rate negotiated individually with a large customer (typically industrial or commercial) rather than a standard tariff rate. True for special contracts; False for standard tariff schedules.']
  tariff_book_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the section, schedule, or page number in the published tariff book where this rate schedule is documented. Example: Schedule E-1, Page 12 of Electric Tariff Book.']
  tier_structure_definition varchar [note: 'JSON or delimited string defining tiered rate blocks for tiered rate structures. Example: Tier 1: 0-500 kWh at $0.10/kWh; Tier 2: 501-1000 kWh at $0.12/kWh; Tier 3: 1001+ kWh at $0.15/kWh. Nullable for non-tiered schedules.']
  tou_period_definition varchar [note: 'JSON or delimited string defining TOU pricing periods and rates. Example: On-Peak (2pm-8pm weekdays): $0.25/kWh; Off-Peak (all other hours): $0.08/kWh; Super Off-Peak (midnight-6am): $0.05/kWh. Nullable for non-TOU schedules.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number for this rate schedule. Increments with each tariff revision or rate case modification. Used to track rate schedule evolution over time.']
  voltage_level varchar [note: 'Voltage level at which service is delivered. Primary (distribution voltage), Secondary (customer voltage), Transmission (high voltage bulk), Sub-Transmission (intermediate voltage). Affects rate level due to cost-of-service differences.']

  Note: 'Authoritative master catalog of all tariff rate schedules applicable to electric and gas service — TOU, CPP, tiered residential, commercial demand, and special contract rates. Defines rate code, commodity type (electric/gas), customer class (residential/commercial/industrial), effective and expiration dates, regulatory approval reference, rate structure type, and base rate values per tier/period. References applicable rider_charge records for surcharges layered on top of base rates. Sourced from PUC-approved tariff filings and maintained in Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U rate engine. SSOT for all base rate definitions used in charge calculation. Distinct from rider_charge, which defines regulatory surcharges approved separately from base tariff rates.'
}

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generated|issued|mailed|paid|partially_paid|disputed|written_off|cancelled — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  invoice_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the invoice based on billing cycle context. Regular invoices are standard monthly/bi-monthly bills.   tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total taxes applied to the invoice, including state sales tax, local utility taxes, franchise fees, and any other government-mandated taxes. Tax rates and applicability vary by jurisdiction and customer class. Expressed in USD.']
  total_amount_due decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total amount the customer must pay, calculated as previous balance plus current charges plus taxes plus regulatory riders. This is the net amount due printed on the invoice. Expressed in USD.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when the invoice record was last modified. Updated when invoice status changes, payments are applied, or adjustments are made. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']

  Note: 'Core billing document representing a single billing cycle statement issued to a customer account for electric and/or gas service. Captures bill period start/end dates, due date, total amount due, prior balance, current charges, taxes, regulatory riders, and net amount. Tracks invoice status (generated, mailed, paid, disputed, written-off). Links to the rate schedule applied, service agreement, and meter read period. Generated from Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U billing engine and posted to SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP for GAAP revenue recognition. SSOT for all customer billing documents.'
}

  disputed_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this invoice line is under customer dispute.   regulatory_rider_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the regulatory rider or surcharge applied to this line. Riders are PUC-approved rate adjustments for specific cost recovery mechanisms.   revenue_class_code varchar [note: 'Customer class or revenue category for regulatory reporting.   revenue_recognition_date date [note: 'Date on which revenue for this invoice line is recognized in the General Ledger under GAAP ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).   service_type varchar [note: 'Type of utility service being billed on this line. ELECTRIC for electric service charges (kWh, kW), GAS for natural gas service charges (MCF, Therm). Enables revenue decomposition by commodity type for regulatory reporting to PUCs and FERC.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record that generated this invoice line. CC&B (Oracle Customer Care and Billing), IS-U (SAP Industry Solution for Utilities), MDMS (Meter Data Management System for interval data charges), ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning for manual adjustments), MANUAL (manually entered adjustments). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and system integration reconciliation.']
  source_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'Unique transaction identifier from the source system (Oracle CC&B, SAP IS-U, or MDMS) that generated this invoice line. Enables traceability back to the originating billing calculation or charge engine transaction. Supports audit trail, dispute resolution, and system integration reconciliation.']
  tax_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Tax amount applied to this invoice line. Includes sales tax, utility tax, franchise fees, or other regulatory taxes. Calculated based on applicable tax rates and jurisdictional rules. Null if the line item is non-taxable or represents a tax charge itself. Supports tax reporting and revenue recognition under GAAP.']
  taxable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this invoice line is subject to sales tax or utility tax. True if taxable, False if exempt. Determines whether tax_amount is calculated for this line. Tax exemption rules vary by jurisdiction, customer class, and charge type. Supports tax compliance and reporting.']
  total_line_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Total amount for this invoice line including taxes. Calculated as line_amount plus tax_amount. Represents the final charge or credit amount for this line item. Positive values indicate charges; negative values indicate credits. Expressed in the invoice currency.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the usage quantity. KWH (kilowatt-hour) for electric energy consumption, MWH (megawatt-hour) for large commercial/industrial energy, KW (kilowatt) for electric demand, MW (megawatt) for large demand, MCF (thousand cubic feet) for natural gas volume, THERM (unit of heat energy) for gas billing, EACH for count-based charges (e.g., number of reconnections), PERCENT for percentage-based adjustments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: KWH|MWH|KW|MW|MCF|THERM|EACH|PERCENT — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  unit_rate decimal(12,6) [note: 'Rate per unit of measure applied to calculate the charge amount. Expressed in currency per unit (e.g., dollars per kWh, dollars per MCF, dollars per kW). Derived from the approved tariff rate schedule filed with the PUC. Null for fixed charges or lump-sum adjustments. Critical for rate case analysis and revenue reconciliation.']
  usage_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of utility service consumed or delivered during the billing period. For energy charges, represents kilowatt-hours (kWh), Megawatt-hours (MWh), thousand cubic feet (MCF), or Therms. For demand charges, represents peak kilowatts (kW) or Megawatts (MW). Null for fixed charges, taxes, or credits that are not usage-based. Sourced from MDMS interval data aggregation or Automated Meter Reading (AMR) systems.']

  Note: 'Itemized charge line within a customer invoice representing a single billable component — energy consumption charges (kWh, MCF, Therm), demand charges (kW), fixed customer charges, distribution rider, FAC adjustment, CIAC recovery, RPS surcharge, taxes, or credits. T']

  Note: 'Record of a financial payment transaction applied against a customer account balance — check, ACH/EFT, credit card, cash, auto-pay, budget billing installment, or third-party agency payment. Integrates with SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP for cash receipts posting and GAAP revenue recognition. SSOT for all customer payment transactions.'

Table billing.payment_arrangement {
  payment_arrangement_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system identifier for the payment arrangement record. Primary key.']
  account_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer account for which this payment arrangement was established. Links to the billing account in Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U.']
  associated_collections_action_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the collections action or case that prompted this payment arrangement. Null if arrangement was proactively requested by customer rather than initiated through collections workflow.']
  actual_completion_date date [note: 'Actual date when the arrangement was fully satisfied and all deferred amounts paid. Null if arrangement is still active, broken, or cancelled. May differ from arrangement_end_date if customer paid early or late.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date when the payment arrangement was formally approved by the utility. May differ from arrangement_start_date if down payment is required before activation.']
  approved_by_user_code varchar [note: 'User ID of the customer service representative, supervisor, or automated system that approved the payment arrangement. Used for audit trail and quality assurance.']
  arrangement_end_date date [note: 'Scheduled date when the final installment is due and the arrangement is expected to be completed. Calculated from start date plus (number_of_installments * installment_frequency).']
  arrangement_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for customer service representatives to document special terms, customer circumstances, or other contextual information relevant to the arrangement. Not displayed to customer.']
  arrangement_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible unique business identifier for the payment arrangement, typically displayed on customer correspondence and used in customer service interactions.']
  arrangement_start_date date [note: 'Effective date when the payment arrangement becomes active and the first installment is due. Typically the date down payment is received or arrangement is approved.']
  arrangement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the payment arrangement. Pending: awaiting approval or down payment. Active: in good standing with payments current. Broken: customer missed payment(s) per terms. Completed: all installments paid. Cancelled: arrangement terminated by utility or customer. Suspended: temporarily paused.']
  arrangement_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payment arrangement plan. Budget billing spreads annual costs evenly; levelized payment smooths seasonal variation; low-income assistance provides subsidized payment terms; collections installment addresses past-due balances; deferred payment postpones a portion of charges; custom represents negotiated terms.']
  auto_pay_enrolled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has enrolled in automatic payment for installments via bank draft or credit card. Auto-pay enrollment often reduces the risk of arrangement default.']
  broken_date date [note: 'Date when the arrangement was marked as broken due to non-compliance with payment terms. Triggers collections workflow and potential service disconnection per tariff rules.']
  cancellation_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code explaining why the arrangement was cancelled before completion. Used for reporting and policy analysis.']
  cancelled_date date [note: 'Date when the arrangement was cancelled by the utility or customer before completion. Remaining balance typically becomes immediately due.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when the payment arrangement record was first created in Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U. Used for audit trail and data lineage.']
  down_payment_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Initial payment required to establish the arrangement, typically a percentage of the total deferred amount as mandated by state Public Utility Commission (PUC) rules or utility policy. Expressed in USD.']
  grace_period_days varchar [note: 'Number of days after installment due date before a missed payment is counted against the arrangement. Typically 5-15 days per utility policy or PUC regulation.']
  installment_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Fixed amount due per installment period, calculated as (total_deferred_amount - down_payment_amount) / number_of_installments. May be adjusted for final installment to account for rounding. Expressed in USD.']
  installment_frequency varchar [note: 'Cadence at which installment payments are due. Monthly is most common for residential customers; other frequencies may be used for commercial accounts or special assistance programs.']
  installments_missed varchar [note: 'Count of scheduled installment payments that were not received by the due date. Exceeding the allowed threshold (typically 1-2 missed payments) triggers arrangement_status transition to broken.']
  installments_paid varchar [note: 'Count of installment payments successfully received and applied to the arrangement. Used to track compliance with payment schedule.']
  interest_accrued decimal(15,2) [note: 'Total interest charges accrued on the deferred balance to date. Zero if interest_rate is zero. Expressed in USD.']
  interest_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Annual interest rate applied to the deferred balance, if any. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 for 5%). Many jurisdictions prohibit interest on residential payment arrangements; commercial arrangements may include interest per tariff.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when the payment arrangement record was last updated. Tracks changes to status, payments applied, or other arrangement attributes.']
  next_installment_due_date date [note: 'Date when the next scheduled installment payment is due. Updated after each payment is received. Null when arrangement is completed, broken, or cancelled.']
  notification_preference varchar [note: 'Customer\'s preferred channel for receiving payment reminders and arrangement status notifications. Used by Customer Information System (CIS) to trigger communications.']
  number_of_installments varchar [note: 'Total count of scheduled installment payments over the life of the arrangement. Typically ranges from 3 to 24 months depending on arrangement type and regulatory constraints.']
  program_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the low-income assistance program, demand-side management (DSM) program, or special rate program under which this arrangement was established. Examples: LIHEAP, CARE, FERA. Null for standard arrangements.']
  remaining_balance decimal(15,2) [note: 'Current outstanding balance under the arrangement after applying all payments received to date. Decreases with each installment payment. Zero when arrangement is completed. Expressed in USD.']
  total_deferred_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Total outstanding balance being deferred under this arrangement at the time of establishment, including principal charges, late fees, and any applicable interest. Expressed in USD.']

  Note: 'Formal deferred payment plan or installment agreement established for a customer account with past-due balance — budget billing plan, levelized payment plan, low-income assistance plan, or collections payment arrangement. Captures arrangement type, total deferred amount, number of installments, installment amount, start date, end date, down payment amount, arrangement status (active, broken, completed, cancelled), and associated collections action. Tracks compliance with arrangement terms to support collections workflow in Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U. Distinct from a single payment transaction — represents an ongoing multi-period commitment.'
}

  budget_billing_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether accounts in this cycle are eligible for budget billing programs, which spread annual costs evenly across monthly payments.']
  commodity_type varchar [note: 'Type of utility service covered by this billing cycle: electric, gas, or dual (combined electric and gas).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this billing cycle record was first created in the Customer Information System (CIS). Used for audit and data lineage tracking.']
  customer_class varchar [note: 'Customer class or segment served by this billing cycle. Determines rate schedule eligibility and billing complexity.']
  cycle_code varchar [note: 'Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the billing cycle within the billing system. Used as the business identifier for cycle assignment and batch scheduling.']
  cycle_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the billing cycle purpose, coverage area, and operational notes. May include territory, route grouping, or special handling instructions.']
  cycle_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which accounts in this cycle are billed. Monthly is standard for residential; bi-monthly, quarterly, or special cycles may apply to large Commercial and Industrial (C&I) accounts.']
  cycle_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name of the billing cycle, such as \'Monthly Residential Cycle 01\' or \'Bi-Monthly Commercial Cycle A\'.']
  cycle_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of the billing cycle. Active cycles are used for new account assignments and ongoing billing operations. Inactive cycles are retained for historical reference.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this billing cycle configuration became or will become effective. Supports versioning and regulatory compliance for cycle changes.']
  estimated_account_count varchar [note: 'Approximate number of customer accounts assigned to this billing cycle. Used for capacity planning, batch sizing, and workload balancing across cycles.']
  estimated_billing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether estimated billing is permitted for accounts in this cycle when actual meter reads are unavailable. Subject to regulatory limits on consecutive estimated bills.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date when this billing cycle configuration expires or was superseded. Null for currently active cycles. Used for historical tracking and regulatory audit.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this billing cycle record was last updated. Tracks configuration changes and supports change management processes.']
  meter_read_end_day varchar [note: 'Day of the month (1-31) when the meter reading window closes for accounts in this cycle. All meter reads must be completed by this day to support timely bill generation.']
  meter_read_start_day varchar [note: 'Day of the month (1-31) when the meter reading window opens for accounts in this cycle. Drives Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) or Automated Meter Reading (AMR) batch scheduling.']
  paperless_billing_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether accounts in this cycle are eligible for paperless billing and electronic invoice delivery. Supports cost reduction and environmental initiatives.']
  payment_due_day varchar [note: 'Target day of the month (1-31) when payment is due for invoices in this cycle. Calculated as bill_date plus payment_due_offset_days.']
  payment_due_offset_days varchar [note: 'Number of days after bill date when payment is due. Typically 15-30 days for residential accounts; may vary by customer class and regulatory requirements.']
  regulatory_approval_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the Public Utility Commission (PUC) docket, order, or tariff filing that approved this billing cycle configuration. Required for regulatory compliance and audit.']
  route_grouping varchar [note: 'Meter reading route or grouping identifier used to organize field meter readers or AMI collection schedules. May represent physical routes or logical batches.']
  special_handling_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this cycle requires special processing, such as manual review, custom rate application, or non-standard billing rules. True for large C&I or wholesale accounts.']
  tariff_book_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the section of the utility tariff book that governs billing cycle assignment and payment terms for this cycle. Used for regulatory compliance and customer dispute resolution.']
  territory_code varchar [note: 'Geographic territory or service area code associated with this billing cycle. Aligns with Geographic Information System (GIS) boundaries and operational districts.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version number of this billing cycle configuration. Incremented when cycle parameters are modified. Supports change tracking and regulatory audit.']

  Note: 'Master definition of billing cycle schedules governing when customer accounts are meter-read and billed — monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly, and special cycles for large C&I accounts. Captures cycle code, cycle description, scheduled meter read window (start day, end day), bill generation date offset from read completion, payment due date offset from bill date, estimated account count per cycle, cycle territory/route grouping, and active/inactive status. Drives batch scheduling of meter reads, bill calculation runs, and payment due date assignment across the billing engine. Referenced by service agreements to assign billing cadence and by invoices to record which cycle generated the bill. Sourced from Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U billing cycle configuration.'
}

Table billing.collections_action {
  collections_action_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for collections_action']
  associated_collections_action_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on collections_action (associated_collections_action_id)']
  action_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the collections action type. Notification includes letters and notices; contact_attempt includes calls and visits; payment_arrangement includes plans and extensions; legal_action includes liens and judgments; service_action includes disconnection and reconnection; account_adjustment includes write-offs and settlements; escalation includes agency referrals; resolution includes payment received and account closure.']
  action_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code representing the type of collections action (e.g., NOTICE_1, CALL_ATTEMPT, PAYMENT_PLAN, DISCONNECT_WARN, SERVICE_SUSPEND). Used as a business identifier for integration with Customer Information System (CIS) and billing workflows.']
  action_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the collections action (e.g., First Delinquency Notice, Payment Arrangement Offer, Service Disconnection Warning, Final Notice Before Shutoff).']
  action_sequence varchar [note: 'Numeric ordering of this action within a standard collections workflow. Lower numbers represent earlier actions in the escalation path (e.g., 1 for first notice, 5 for final notice, 10 for disconnection).']
  applicable_customer_class varchar [note: 'Customer segment(s) to which this collections action applies. Residential for household customers; commercial for small/medium business; industrial for large commercial and manufacturing; all for universal actions. Different customer classes may have different regulatory protections and collections workflows.']

True for system-automated actions; false for manual-only actions requiring human review.']
  auto_trigger_rule varchar [note: 'Business rule or condition that automatically triggers this collections action. Examples: \'Balance > $100 AND Days Past Due >= 30\', \'Second missed payment on payment plan\', \'No response to prior notice within 15 days\'. Null if action is manual-only.']
  cost_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'Standard cost or fee associated with executing this collections action, charged to the customer account. Includes costs such as certified mail fees, field visit charges, reconnection fees, or collection agency commissions. Null if no cost is assessed.']
  cost_recoverable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the cost of this collections action can be billed to and recovered from the customer account. True if cost is customer-billable; false if cost is absorbed by the utility as a business expense.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this collections action record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  credit_reporting_impact varchar [note: 'Indicates the impact of this collections action on customer credit bureau reporting. None for actions with no credit impact; negative_report for delinquency or charge-off reporting; positive_report for successful payment plan completion; dispute_flag for contested accounts.']
  delivery_method varchar [note: 'The channel or medium through which the collections action is delivered to the customer. Mail for standard postal delivery; certified_mail for proof-of-delivery requirements; email and sms for electronic notifications; phone_call for voice contact; in_person for field visits; portal_notification for customer self-service alerts.']
  description varchar [note: 'Detailed business description of the collections action, including purpose, typical use cases, and any special handling instructions. Provides context for collections staff and system administrators.']
  dispute_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the customer has the right to dispute or appeal this collections action. True for actions subject to customer dispute rights; false for non-disputable administrative actions.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date on which this collections action definition is retired or superseded. Null for currently active actions. Used for historical analysis and regulatory audit trails.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date from which this collections action definition becomes active and available for use in collections workflows. Used for version control and regulatory compliance tracking.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this collections action record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.']
  legal_action_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action involves or initiates legal proceedings (e.g., filing a lien, initiating small claims, referring to attorney). True for legal actions; false for operational collections activities.']
  minimum_notice_days varchar [note: 'Minimum number of days required by regulation between this action and any subsequent service disconnection or legal action. Null if no regulatory minimum applies. Varies by jurisdiction and customer class (residential vs. commercial).']
  modified_by_user varchar [note: 'User identifier or name of the person who last modified this collections action definition. Used for accountability and audit trail purposes.']
  payment_plan_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether customers receiving this collections action are eligible to enter into a payment arrangement or installment plan to avoid further escalation. True if payment plan option is available; false if account is past payment plan eligibility.']
  protected_customer_exempt boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action is prohibited for protected customer categories (e.g., medical necessity customers, low-income assistance participants, elderly or disabled customers with special protections). True if action cannot be applied to protected customers; false if action is universally applicable.']
  regulatory_notice_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action must comply with state or federal regulatory notice requirements (e.g., minimum notice periods before disconnection, specific language mandates, customer rights disclosures). True for actions subject to Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) rules.']
  regulatory_reference varchar [note: 'Citation of the specific state Public Utility Commission (PUC) rule, tariff section, or federal regulation that governs this collections action. Examples: \'PUC Rule 25.483\', \'Tariff Section 6.2.1\', \'FERC Order 2222\'. Null if no specific regulatory mandate applies.']
  requires_customer_response boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action requires an explicit response or action from the customer (e.g., payment, contact, dispute filing). True for actions requiring customer engagement; false for informational or system-driven actions.']
  requires_supervisor_approval boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action requires managerial or supervisory approval before execution. True for high-impact actions such as disconnection, legal referral, or large write-offs; false for routine automated actions.']
  response_due_days varchar [note: 'Number of days from action delivery date by which the customer must respond or take action. Null if no response deadline applies. Used to calculate follow-up action triggers and compliance with regulatory notice periods.']
  seasonal_restriction_applies boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action is subject to seasonal restrictions (e.g., winter moratorium on disconnections, extreme weather protections). True if action is restricted during certain months or weather conditions; false if action can be taken year-round.']
  service_action_type varchar [note: 'Specifies the type of field service action triggered by this collections action. Disconnect for service termination; reconnect for service restoration; meter_lock for physical access prevention; meter_removal for complete meter extraction; limiter_install for reduced service capacity; none if no service action is triggered.']
  severity_level varchar [note: 'Indicates the urgency and escalation level of the collections action. Informational for early reminders; low for initial notices; medium for follow-up actions; high for pre-disconnection warnings; critical for imminent service termination; final for last action before legal or agency referral.']
  status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this collections action definition. Active for in-use actions; inactive for temporarily disabled actions; suspended for actions under regulatory review; retired for obsolete actions retained for historical reference.']
  template_document_code varchar [note: 'Reference identifier for the standard letter, notice, or script template used for this collections action. Links to document management system for content retrieval and version control. Null if no template is used (e.g., for system-automated actions).']
  third_party_agency_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether accounts subject to this collections action are eligible for referral to external collection agencies. True if action can trigger agency placement; false if action must remain internal.']
  triggers_service_action boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this collections action directly triggers a field service action such as disconnection, reconnection, or meter lock. True for actions that initiate service orders; false for administrative or notification-only actions.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for collections_action. Referenced by associated_collections_action_id.'
}
