  issuing_person_name varchar [note: 'Name of the warehouse clerk or storekeeper who physically issued the material from inventory.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this goods issue record was last modified or updated in the system.']

  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes or comments related to the goods issue transaction, capturing special handling instructions, exceptions, or additional context.']

  priority_code varchar [note: 'Priority level of the goods issue request, used for expediting critical work orders or emergency restoration activities.']
  receiving_cost_object_type varchar [note: 'The type of cost object receiving the material: work order (maintenance), CAPEX project (capital construction), cost center (operational expense), or asset (capitalization).']

  reversal_indicator boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this goods issue has been reversed (movement type 262). True if reversed, False otherwise.']

  serial_number varchar [note: 'Serial number for individually tracked materials or equipment, enabling asset-level traceability.']
  storage_location_code varchar [note: 'The specific storage location code within the warehouse from which the material was issued.']
  storm_event_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier for the storm or emergency event if this goods issue is related to storm restoration or emergency response activities. Critical for tracking storm restoration material consumption for regulatory cost recovery.']

  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for the issued quantity (e.g., EA for each, FT for feet, LB for pounds, GAL for gallons).']
  valuation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total monetary value of the issued material calculated using standard cost or moving average price. This is the principal monetary fact for cost accounting.']
  wbs_element varchar [note: 'The WBS element or network activity to which the material cost is charged for project-based consumption (movement type 281).']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing the physical issuance and consumption of materials from inventory stock against a work order, CAPEX project, cost center, or material reservation. Records goods issue document number, posting date, material reference (linked to material_master), issuing storage location (linked to warehouse), reservation reference (linked to material_reservation), receiving cost object (work order, WBS element, cost center, or asset number), issued quantity, unit of measure, movement type (261 goods issue for order, 262 reversal of goods issue, 201 goods issue for cost center, 281 goods issue for network/project), batch/lot number for traceable materials, issuing warehouse clerk, and SAP material document number. Triggers inventory stock position reduction and drives actual material cost posting to work orders and CAPEX projects. Critical for closing the inventory movement lifecycle (goods_receipt IN → material_reservation COMMIT → goods_issue OUT), supporting three-way match completion, work order costing, storm restoration material consumption tracking, and FERC/PUC cost reporting for rate case filings.'
}

Table regulatory.docket {
  docket_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each regulatory docket or proceeding record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.']
  appeal_deadline_date date [note: 'The deadline by which a party must file a request for rehearing, appeal, or petition for review of the final order. Calculated from the final order date based on applicable statutory or regulatory timelines (e.g., 30 days for FERC rehearing requests under FPA Section 313). Null if no final order has been issued.']
  appeal_filed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the utility or any party has filed an appeal, request for rehearing, or petition for review of the final order in this docket. True if an appeal or rehearing request has been filed; False otherwise. Null if the docket has not yet reached a final order. Used to track post-order litigation exposure and contingent liability.']
  approved_rate_of_return decimal(6,4) [note: 'The overall rate of return on equity (ROE) approved by the regulatory authority in the final order, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0975 for 9.75%). Null until a final order is issued or if the proceeding is not a rate case. Critical for financial planning, EBITDA projections, and investor reporting.']
  approved_revenue_requirement decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total annual revenue requirement approved by the regulatory authority in the final order for a rate case, expressed in U.S. dollars. Null until a final order is issued or if the proceeding is not a rate case. Used for rate design, billing system updates, and financial reporting under GAAP and SOX.']
  case_manager varchar [note: 'Full name of the regulatory affairs case manager or project manager responsible for coordinating the utility\'s internal response, testimony preparation, and milestone tracking for this docket. Typically a regulatory affairs department employee.']
  close_date date [note: 'The date on which the regulatory authority formally closed the docket, typically upon issuance of a final order, dismissal, or withdrawal. Null if the docket remains open or active. Used to calculate proceeding duration and track regulatory cycle times.']
  confidential_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the utility has requested confidential treatment for some or all documents filed in this docket under applicable protective order or FOIA exemption. True if confidential treatment has been requested; False if all filings are public. Used to enforce data access controls and document management policies.']
  cpcn_project_name varchar [note: 'The name of the capital project or infrastructure investment for which a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) is being sought. Applicable only to CPCN proceedings. Examples: \'North Substation 345kV Upgrade\', \'Gas Pipeline Replacement Phase 2\'. Null for non-CPCN dockets.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this docket record was first created in the regulatory case management system or data lakehouse. Represents the audit trail creation event. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.']
  customer_class_scope varchar [note: 'Identifies the customer class(es) affected by this regulatory proceeding. For rate cases and tariff filings, indicates whether the proceeding impacts residential, commercial, industrial, or all customer classes. \'none\' is used for proceedings that do not directly affect customer rates (e.g., NERC reliability compliance).']
  docket_number varchar [note: 'The official externally-assigned docket or case number issued by the jurisdictional authority (e.g., PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA). This is the primary business identifier used in all regulatory correspondence, filings, and orders. Examples: FERC Docket No. ER24-1234, PUC Case No. 24-0001-EL-RDR.']
  docket_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the regulatory docket or proceeding. \'open\' indicates the docket has been initiated but no active proceedings are underway; \'active\' indicates proceedings are actively ongoing; \'suspended\' indicates proceedings are temporarily halted by order or stipulation; \'closed\' indicates the proceeding has concluded with a final order or disposition; \'withdrawn\' indicates the utility voluntarily withdrew the filing.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which the rates, tariff provisions, or regulatory requirements approved in this docket become effective and binding. For rate cases, this is the date new rates go into effect. For tariff filings, this is the tariff effective date. May be subject to refund if rates are accepted subject to refund under FERC practice.']
  estimated_capex decimal(18,2) [note: 'The estimated capital expenditure (CAPEX) associated with the project or investment subject to this regulatory proceeding, expressed in U.S. dollars. Relevant for CPCN applications, IRP submissions, and major infrastructure rate cases. Used for prudency review tracking and AFUDC calculation. Null for proceedings not involving capital investment.']
  filing_date date [note: 'The date on which the utility filed the initial application, petition, or complaint with the regulatory authority. This is the principal business event date for the docket — the date the proceeding was formally initiated. Used for tracking regulatory deadlines, statutory timelines, and compliance milestones.']
  final_order_date date [note: 'The date on which the regulatory authority issued the final order, decision, or ruling concluding the proceeding. Null if the docket is still open or active. Used to calculate total proceeding duration, track regulatory cycle times, and trigger downstream actions such as billing system rate updates and financial reporting.']
  ghg_program_ref varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific GHG compliance program or emissions regulation at issue in an EPA or state environmental compliance docket (e.g., \'EPA Clean Air Act Section 111(d)\', \'State GHG Cap-and-Trade Program\', \'RPS Compliance\'). Applicable to GHG and emissions compliance proceedings. Null for non-environmental dockets.']
  hearing_date date [note: 'The scheduled or actual start date of the formal evidentiary hearing before the regulatory authority or administrative law judge (ALJ). Null if no hearing is required or if the hearing has not yet been scheduled. Used for legal resource scheduling and milestone tracking.']
  hearing_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the regulatory authority has ordered or is expected to require a formal evidentiary hearing (trial-type proceeding) for this docket. True if a hearing has been ordered or is anticipated; False if the proceeding is expected to be resolved on the written record. Impacts resource planning for testimony preparation and witness scheduling.']
  intervenor_count varchar [note: 'The number of parties that have been granted intervenor status in the regulatory proceeding. Intervenors may include consumer advocates, industrial customers, environmental groups, competing utilities, and municipal entities. A higher intervenor count typically signals a more complex and contested proceeding. Updated as the proceeding progresses.']
  irp_planning_horizon_years varchar [note: 'The planning horizon in years covered by an Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submission. Typically 10, 15, or 20 years. Applicable only to IRP dockets. Used to track long-range resource adequacy planning obligations and RPS compliance trajectories. Null for non-IRP proceedings.']
  jurisdiction varchar [note: 'The specific jurisdictional scope of the docket — identifies the state, federal, or regional authority. For state PUC proceedings, this is the two-letter state abbreviation (e.g., OH, CA, TX). For federal proceedings, this is \'FEDERAL\'. For regional reliability proceedings, this is the NERC region (e.g., RFC, SERC, WECC).']
  lead_attorney varchar [note: 'Full name of the lead regulatory attorney responsible for managing the utility\'s legal strategy and filings in this docket. Sourced from the legal department\'s matter management system. Used for workload tracking, attorney assignment reporting, and legal resource planning.']
  nerc_standard_ref varchar [note: 'The specific NERC reliability standard(s) at issue in a NERC compliance investigation or reliability proceeding (e.g., \'FAC-001-3\', \'CIP-007-6\', \'TPL-001-4\'). Applicable only to NERC reliability and compliance dockets. Null for non-NERC proceedings. Used for NERC compliance tracking and BES reliability reporting.']
  open_date date [note: 'The date on which the regulatory authority formally opened or docketed the proceeding. May differ from the filing date if the authority assigns a docket number on a date subsequent to the initial filing. Marks the official commencement of the regulatory proceeding.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Internal priority classification assigned by the regulatory affairs department to indicate the strategic and financial significance of the docket to the utility. \'critical\' indicates proceedings with major rate impact or compliance risk; \'high\' indicates significant proceedings; \'medium\' indicates routine proceedings; \'low\' indicates minor or administrative filings. Used for resource allocation and executive reporting.']
  proceeding_subtype varchar [note: 'Further classification within the proceeding type. For example, within a rate case: electric general rate case, gas general rate case, transmission rate case (OATT). Within tariff filings: initial tariff, tariff amendment, tariff cancellation. Provides granular categorization for reporting and analytics.']
  proceeding_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the regulatory proceeding or filing type. Defines the nature and purpose of the docket. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rate_case|cpcn|tariff_filing|irp|rulemaking|complaint|prudency_review|compliance_investigation|pbr|ghg_compliance|nerc_reliability|ppa_approval — promote to reference product]']
  rate_case_type varchar [note: 'Specifies the type of rate case proceeding. \'general\' is a full cost-of-service rate case; \'limited\' is a focused rate case on specific cost elements; \'formula\' is a rate case using a pre-approved formula rate mechanism (common in FERC transmission); \'pbr\' is a Performance-Based Ratemaking proceeding; \'settlement\' is a negotiated settlement rate case. Null for non-rate-case dockets.']
  regulatory_body varchar [note: 'The jurisdictional authority or governing body with which the docket is filed or by which it is assigned. Identifies the primary regulator overseeing the proceeding. Values include FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission), PUC (Public Utility Commission), NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation), EPA (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency), PHMSA (Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration), DOE (U.S. Department of Energy), OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FERC|PUC|NERC|EPA|PHMSA|DOE|OSHA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  requested_rate_of_return decimal(6,4) [note: 'The overall rate of return on equity (ROE) requested by the utility in a rate case, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1050 for 10.50%). Null for non-rate-case proceedings. Used in rate case analytics, benchmarking against peer utilities, and PBR performance tracking.']
  requested_revenue_requirement decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total annual revenue requirement requested by the utility in a rate case filing, expressed in U.S. dollars. Represents the utility\'s claimed cost of service including OPEX, CAPEX recovery (depreciation), AFUDC, taxes, and allowed return on equity (ROE). Null for non-rate-case proceedings. This is a pre-decision requested amount, not the approved amount.']
  rto_iso_ref varchar [note: 'Identifies the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) relevant to this docket, if applicable. Examples: PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE. Relevant for FERC transmission rate cases, OATT filings, and market rule proceedings. Null for state-only or non-transmission proceedings.']
  service_type varchar [note: 'Identifies whether the docket pertains to electric service, gas service, or both. Used to route dockets to the appropriate regulatory, legal, and operations teams and to support domain-specific regulatory reporting.']
  settlement_date date [note: 'The date on which the settlement agreement was executed or filed with the regulatory authority. Null if no settlement was reached. Used in conjunction with settlement_reached to track the timeline of negotiated resolutions and their impact on proceeding duration.']
  settlement_reached boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the parties in the regulatory proceeding reached a negotiated settlement agreement in lieu of a fully litigated final order. True if a settlement was filed and approved; False if the proceeding was fully litigated or is still pending. Used to track settlement rates and litigation complexity across the regulatory docket portfolio.']
  statutory_deadline_date date [note: 'The date by which the regulatory authority is legally required to issue a final order or decision under applicable statute or rule. For example, FERC has a 60-day default effective date for rate filings under FPA Section 205; state PUCs may have statutory deadlines for rate case decisions. Null if no statutory deadline applies.']
  subject_matter_summary varchar [note: 'A concise narrative description of the subject matter, issues, and relief sought in the regulatory proceeding. Provides business context for users who need to understand the docket without reviewing the full filing. Sourced from the utility\'s regulatory affairs case management system or the regulatory authority\'s docket management system.']
  test_year varchar [note: 'The test year or test period used as the basis for cost-of-service calculations in a rate case. May be a historical test year (e.g., \'2023\'), a future test year (e.g., \'2025\'), or a hybrid period (e.g., \'2023-2024\'). Null for non-rate-case proceedings. Fundamental to rate case analytics and cost allocation studies.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this docket record was most recently modified in the regulatory case management system or data lakehouse. Used for change data capture (CDC), ETL incremental loads, and audit trail compliance. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.']
  utility_division varchar [note: 'The utility operating division or service territory to which this docket primarily applies. Distinguishes between electric distribution, gas distribution, transmission, generation, or combined proceedings. Critical for segregating regulatory obligations by business unit and for rate case cost allocation.']

  Note: 'Master record for each regulatory docket or proceeding filed with or assigned by a jurisdictional authority (PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA, PHMSA). Captures docket number, proceeding type (rate case, CPCN, tariff filing, IRP, rulemaking, complaint, prudency review, compliance investigation), filing jurisdiction, assigned regulatory body, docket status (open, active, suspended, closed), open/close dates, lead attorney, associated case manager, and key milestone dates. Serves as the SSOT anchor for all regulatory proceedings — the central hub to which rate cases, filings, orders, CPCN applications, IRP submissions, and prudency reviews connect.'
}

Table regulatory.rate_case {
  rate_case_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each rate case or rate proceeding record in the system. Serves as the primary key for the rate_case data product.']
  docket_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent regulatory docket under which this rate case is filed. Links the rate case to its governing docket record for full proceeding traceability.']
  test_year_financial_period_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Rate cases use specific financial periods as test years for revenue requirement calculations. Finance teams extract closed period actuals for rate case cost studies. Direct period linkage enables auto']
  afudc_rate_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) rate approved or proposed in this rate case, expressed as a percentage. AFUDC capitalizes the cost of financing construction work in progress (WIP) and is a component of rate base.']
  approved_rate_base decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total rate base authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order, expressed in US dollars. Reflects any disallowances, exclusions, or adjustments made by the regulator to the utility\'s requested rate base.']
  approved_rates_effective_date date [note: 'Date on which the final approved rates became effective for billing purposes. May differ from the final order date if the order specifies a prospective effective date or if rates are subject to a tariff filing lag.']
  approved_revenue_requirement decimal(18,2) [note: 'Final annual revenue requirement authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order, expressed in US dollars. May differ from the requested amount due to regulatory adjustments, disallowances, or settlements.']
  approved_roe_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Return on Equity (ROE) percentage authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order. The approved ROE directly determines the equity return component of the utility\'s allowed revenue requirement.']
  approved_wacc_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) percentage authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order. Reflects the approved blended cost of debt and equity used to compute the authorized return on rate base.']
  case_name varchar [note: 'Official descriptive name or title of the rate case as filed with the regulatory authority (e.g., \'General Rate Case 2024 — Electric Distribution\'). Used for identification in regulatory filings and internal reporting.']
  case_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the rate case proceeding. Tracks progression from initial filing through regulatory review, interim rate authorization, final order issuance, and case closure or appeal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|pending|suspended|interim_rates_in_effect|final_order_issued|closed|appealed — promote to reference product]']
  case_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the rate proceeding by regulatory scope and commodity. Distinguishes general rate cases from transmission-only, gas distribution, electric distribution, formula rate, or limited-scope proceedings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: general_rate_case|transmission_rate_case|gas_distribution_rate_case|electric_distribution_rate_case|formula_rate_case|limited_rate_case|cost_of_service|PBR_only — promote to reference product]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp indicating when this rate case record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the regulatory data product.']
  debt_ratio_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Approved long-term debt percentage of the capital structure as authorized in the final order. Together with equity_ratio_pct defines the approved capital structure for rate-setting purposes.']
  equity_ratio_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Approved equity percentage of the capital structure as authorized in the final order. Together with the debt ratio, defines the capital structure used to compute the weighted average cost of capital and allowed return.']
  fac_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rate case includes or establishes a Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) mechanism allowing automatic pass-through of fuel cost changes between rate cases. True = FAC mechanism included; False = no FAC.']
  filing_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the rate case application or tariff filing was formally submitted to the regulatory authority. Establishes the official start of the regulatory proceeding and triggers statutory review deadlines.']
  filing_jurisdiction_state varchar [note: 'Two-letter US state code identifying the state PUC jurisdiction where this rate case is filed (e.g., \'CA\', \'TX\', \'NY\'). Null for FERC-only proceedings.']
  final_order_date date [note: 'Date on which the regulatory authority issued the final order concluding the rate case proceeding. Marks the official end of the adjudicatory phase and establishes the effective date for approved rates.']
  interim_rate_effective_date date [note: 'Date on which interim rates became effective pending the final order. Interim rates are provisional rates authorized by the regulator to allow the utility to begin collecting adjusted revenues before the proceeding concludes.']
  interim_revenue_requirement decimal(18,2) [note: 'Annual revenue requirement authorized on an interim basis pending the final order, expressed in US dollars. Subject to refund or true-up adjustment once the final order is issued.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing supplementary information, regulatory conditions, compliance obligations, or material facts associated with the rate case that are not captured in structured fields (e.g., specific disallowances, conditions of approval, appeal status details).']
  pbr_actual_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'Actual measured performance value achieved by the utility for the PBR metric during the measurement period. Compared against pbr_target_value to determine variance and calculate earned incentives or assessed penalties.']
  pbr_incentive_penalty_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Dollar amount of the earned incentive (positive) or assessed penalty (negative) resulting from the PBR performance variance for the measurement period. Directly impacts the utility\'s allowed revenue recovery.']
  pbr_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rate case includes a Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) component with defined metrics, targets, and incentive/penalty mechanisms. True = PBR component present; False = traditional cost-of-service only.']
  pbr_measurement_period_end date [note: 'End date of the PBR performance measurement period. Together with pbr_measurement_period_start defines the evaluation window for PBR metric assessment.']
  pbr_measurement_period_start date [note: 'Start date of the PBR performance measurement period during which the utility\'s actual performance is evaluated against approved targets. Populated only when pbr_indicator is True.']
  pbr_metric_type varchar [note: 'Type of PBR performance metric tracked in this rate case. Common metrics include SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index), SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index), CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index), customer satisfaction scores, renewable integration percentage, Energy Efficiency (EE) savings, and Demand Response (DR) curtailment. Populated only when pbr_indicator is True. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAIDI|SAIFI|CAIDI|customer_satisfaction|renewable_integration_pct|EE_savings|DR_curtailment|GHG_emissions — promote to reference product]']
  pbr_target_value decimal(18,4) [note: 'Approved target value for the PBR metric defined in pbr_metric_type for the measurement period. Represents the performance threshold the utility must achieve to earn incentives or avoid penalties (e.g., SAIDI target of 90 minutes, customer satisfaction score of 85).']
  pbr_variance decimal(18,4) [note: 'Calculated variance between the PBR actual value and the PBR target value (actual minus target). A positive variance may indicate over-performance (incentive-eligible) or under-performance depending on the metric direction convention.']
  regulatory_jurisdiction varchar [note: 'Identifies the jurisdictional authority governing this rate case: FERC for interstate transmission and wholesale rates, state PUC for retail distribution rates, or dual for proceedings with both jurisdictional components.']
  requested_rate_base decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total rate base (net plant in service plus working capital allowances) requested by the utility in its filing, expressed in US dollars. Rate base is the foundation for calculating the allowed return on equity and overall revenue requirement.']
  requested_revenue_requirement decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total annual revenue requirement requested by the utility in its initial rate case filing, expressed in US dollars. Represents the total cost of service the utility seeks to recover through rates, including O&M, depreciation, taxes, and return on rate base.']
  requested_roe_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Return on Equity (ROE) percentage requested by the utility in its rate case filing. Represents the equity return component of the weighted average cost of capital used to calculate the allowed return on rate base.']
  requested_wacc_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) percentage requested by the utility, reflecting the blended cost of debt and equity in the proposed capital structure. Used to calculate the overall allowed return on rate base.']
  settlement_date date [note: 'Date on which the settlement agreement was executed by all parties. Populated only when settlement_indicator is True. Used to track the timeline of negotiated resolutions.']
  settlement_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the rate case was resolved through a negotiated settlement agreement between the utility and intervening parties rather than a fully litigated final order. True = settled; False = fully litigated.']
  test_year_end_date date [note: 'End date of the test year used to establish the revenue requirement and rate base. Together with test_year_start_date defines the 12-month test period for cost-of-service analysis.']
  test_year_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the test year (historical or future) used to establish the revenue requirement and rate base in this rate case. The test year is the 12-month period whose costs and revenues form the basis for rate-setting.']
  test_year_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the test year is based on historical recorded data, a future projected period, or a hybrid combining historical actuals with known and measurable adjustments.']
  true_up_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Dollar amount of the true-up adjustment calculated as the difference between interim rates collected and the final approved revenue requirement. A positive value indicates a refund owed to customers; a negative value indicates additional recovery owed to the utility.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp indicating when this rate case record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.']

  Note: 'Master record for each general rate case or rate proceeding filed with a state PUC or FERC. Tracks test year, filing date, requested revenue requirement, allowed ROE, rate base, capital structure, final approved rates, effective date, and interim rate/true-up adjustments. For proceedings with Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) components, captures PBR metric definitions (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, customer satisfaction, renewable integration %, EE savings, DR curtailment), approved target values, measurement periods, actual performance values, variance calculations, and earned incentive or assessed penalty amounts per measurement period. Links to parent docket. Serves as the SSOT for the complete rate case lifecycle from filing through final order, including all PBR performance tracking and incentive/penalty calculations. Critical for revenue requirement management, cost recovery authorization, and regulatory performance reporting.'
}

  schedule_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the tariff schedule by service and rate design category.   testimony_subject varchar [note: 'Describes the primary regulatory topic addressed by the testimony. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: revenue_requirement|rate_design|capital_structure|depreciation|demand_forecast|cost_of_capital|pbr|dsm|ghg_compliance|fuel_adjustment — promote to reference product]']
  testimony_type varchar [note: 'For testimony filings, classifies the stage of the evidentiary record at which the testimony is submitted. \'direct\' is the initial witness statement; \'rebuttal\' responds to opposing direct testimony; \'surrebuttal\' responds to rebuttal testimony; \'errata\' corrects errors in previously filed testimony. Null for non-testimony filings.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this filing record in the regulatory data management system. Used to detect changes, support incremental ETL processing, and maintain audit trail integrity.']
  witness_affiliation varchar [note: 'Organizational affiliation of the testifying witness, indicating which party in the proceeding the witness represents. Distinguishes utility witnesses from intervenor, PUC staff, and independent expert witnesses for evidentiary record management.']
  witness_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the expert witness sponsoring the testimony filing. Populated only for testimony-type filings. Used to track the evidentiary record and cross-examination schedule in rate cases and contested proceedings.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of each formal document or submission filed with a regulatory body (PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA, DOE, PHMSA). Captures filing type (initial application, testimony, exhibit, compliance filing, annual report, NERC reliability standard filing, EPA emissions report), filing date, filer name, filing status (draft, submitted, accepted, rejected, superseded), regulatory body, associated docket, document reference number, and confidentiality designation. For testimony filings (direct, rebuttal, surrebuttal, errata), additionally captures witness name, witness affiliation (utility, intervenor, PUC staff, independent expert), testimony subject matter (revenue requirement, rate design, capital structure, depreciation, demand forecast), exhibit list, and cross-examination schedule. Links to parent docket. Serves as the SSOT for all documents submitted to regulatory authorities, including the complete evidentiary testimony record for rate cases and contested proceedings.'
}

  review_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned by the regulatory body or internal tracking system to uniquely reference this prudency review (e.g., PR-2024-0042).   review_period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the expenditure period under review. Defines the close of the time window for which costs are being evaluated for prudency.']

  review_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the prudency review workflow. Progresses from initiated through in-progress, preliminary finding, final determination, and closure. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.']
  review_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the prudency review by the category of expenditure under examination. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS classification dimension.']
  reviewing_body varchar [note: 'The party or organization conducting the prudency review — e.g., PUC Staff, FERC Staff, an independent auditor appointed by the commission, or Office of Attorney General staff. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category (regulatory reviewer as the counterparty).']
  reviewing_body_name varchar [note: 'Full legal or organizational name of the entity conducting the prudency review (e.g., \'California Public Utilities Commission Division of Ratepayer Advocates\', \'Navigant Consulting Inc.\'). Complements reviewing_body code with a human-readable label for reporting and correspondence.']
  scope_description varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the scope of the prudency review, including the specific projects, programs, time periods, and expenditure categories under examination. Provides context for regulatory testimony and rate case filings.']
  settlement_date date [note: 'Date on which the settlement agreement was executed or approved by the commission, if the prudency review was resolved through settlement. Null if settlement_indicator is False.']
  settlement_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the prudency review was resolved through a negotiated settlement agreement rather than a litigated final order. True if settled; False if resolved by contested commission order.']
  total_expenditure_under_review_amt decimal(18,2) [note: 'Aggregate total expenditure in USD across all cost categories (CAPEX + OPEX + fuel) submitted for prudency review. This is the gross amount subject to the regulatory determination. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER MONETARY_TRIPLET gross-base amount category.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this prudency review record was last modified in the data platform. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.']
  utility_witness_name varchar [note: 'Name of the primary utility witness or subject matter expert who provided testimony or documentation in support of the prudency of the expenditures under review. Used for regulatory proceeding tracking and testimony management.']
  wip_balance_amt decimal(18,2) [note: 'Dollar amount of Work in Progress (WIP) balance associated with the capital project under prudency review at the time of review initiation. Relevant for capital project prudency reviews to assess the in-service conversion and rate base eligibility.']

  Note: 'Master record for each prudency review or management audit initiated by a PUC or FERC to evaluate the reasonableness of utility expenditures for cost recovery. Captures review type (capital project prudency, O&M prudency, fuel cost prudency, storm cost recovery), triggering docket, review scope description, total expenditure under review (CAPEX/OPEX), reviewer identity (PUC staff, independent auditor), preliminary finding, final determination (prudent/imprudent/partial), disallowed amount, and effective date of determination.'

  next_true_up_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next true-up reconciliation filing with the regulatory body. Supports proactive compliance monitoring and workload planning.']

  prudency_review_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether costs recovered under this mechanism are subject to a regulatory prudency review before final recovery is confirmed. True = prudency review required; False = costs are pre-approved without individual prudency review.']
  prudency_review_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the prudency review for costs recovered under this mechanism: not_required = no review required; pending = review not yet initiated; in_progress = review underway; completed = review finalized; disallowed = costs partially or fully disallowed; approved = costs found prudent and approved for full recovery.']
  rate_base_treatment varchar [note: 'Regulatory accounting treatment of costs recovered under this mechanism with respect to the utility\'s rate base: included = costs are part of the approved rate base; excluded = costs are recovered outside rate base as a rider; deferred = costs are deferred pending future rate case inclusion; amortized = costs are being amortized over an approved period.']
  rate_effective_date date [note: 'Date on which the current_rate_amount became effective for billing purposes. Changes when a true-up or rate adjustment is approved.']
  recovery_method varchar [note: 'The billing methodology by which costs are recovered from customers: volumetric = per kWh or MCF consumed; fixed_charge = flat monthly charge per customer; percentage_of_bill = surcharge as a percentage of base bill; demand_charge = per kW of peak demand.']
  recovery_period_months varchar [note: 'Total approved recovery period in months over which the authorized costs are to be collected from customers. For amortized mechanisms, this defines the amortization schedule length.']
  regulatory_asset_liability varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this mechanism creates a regulatory asset (under-recovery, costs deferred for future collection), a regulatory liability (over-recovery, amounts owed back to customers), or neither (pass-through with no balance accumulation).   regulatory_body varchar [note: 'Name of the specific regulatory authority that approved and oversees this cost recovery mechanism (e.g., \'Texas PUC\', \'California PUC\', \'FERC\', \'Illinois Commerce Commission\').']
  service_type varchar [note: 'Utility service type to which this cost recovery mechanism applies: electric distribution, gas distribution, or combined electric and gas service.']
  tariff_schedule_ref varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific tariff schedule, rate schedule, or tariff sheet number in the utility\'s filed tariff that implements this cost recovery mechanism. Used to cross-reference the regulatory authorization with the billing rate schedule.']
  total_authorized_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total dollar amount authorized by the regulatory body for recovery under this mechanism over its full approved life. Null for open-ended mechanisms without a defined total cap. Expressed in USD.']
  true_up_frequency varchar [note: 'Regulatory-approved frequency at which the cost recovery mechanism balance is reconciled and rates are adjusted to correct for over- or under-recovery (e.g., monthly for FAC, annual for infrastructure riders).']
  wip_balance decimal(18,2) [note: 'Current construction Work in Progress balance associated with this AFUDC or infrastructure rider mechanism. Applicable when mechanism_type is AFUDC or infrastructure_rider. Expressed in USD. Null for non-capital mechanisms.']

  Note: 'Master record for each approved regulatory cost recovery mechanism or rider in effect for the utility. Covers FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause), AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction), CIAC (Contribution in Aid of Construction), infrastructure riders, storm cost recovery trackers, and DSM/EE program cost recovery mechanisms.   internal_audit_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the internal audit report or compliance assessment that identified the deficiency requiring corrective action.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this corrective action plan record was most recently modified or updated.']
  milestone_count varchar [note: 'Total number of discrete milestones or action items defined within the corrective action plan.']
  milestones_completed_count varchar [note: 'Number of milestones that have been completed and verified as of the current reporting date.']
  penalty_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Monetary penalty in USD assessed by the regulatory authority for the underlying violation, which may be mitigated or waived based on corrective action plan completion.']
  penalty_mitigation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether successful completion of the corrective action plan resulted in reduction or waiver of the assessed penalty.']
  percent_complete decimal(5,2) [note: 'Overall completion percentage of the corrective action plan, calculated as (milestones_completed_count / milestone_count) * 100.']
  plan_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative describing the corrective actions, remediation steps, process improvements, and controls to be implemented to address the identified deficiency or violation.']
  plan_number varchar [note: 'Business identifier for the corrective action plan, typically assigned by the regulatory body or internal compliance system.']
  plan_owner_email varchar [note: 'Email address of the individual or team responsible for day-to-day management and execution of the corrective action plan.']
  plan_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the corrective action plan indicating its stage in the regulatory review and implementation process.']
  plan_title varchar [note: 'Descriptive title or name of the corrective action plan summarizing the remediation focus.']
  prudency_review_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the corrective action plan costs are subject to a prudency review by the regulatory commission to determine cost recovery eligibility.']
  recurrence_risk_level varchar [note: 'Assessment of the likelihood that the underlying violation or non-compliance issue will recur after corrective actions are implemented.']
  regulatory_authority varchar [note: 'The governing body or regulatory agency that mandated or is overseeing the corrective action plan (e.g., FERC, state PUC, NERC, EPA).']
  regulatory_filing_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier of the formal regulatory filing or submission that included or documented this corrective action plan.']
  responsible_department varchar [note: 'The internal department, business unit, or functional area responsible for executing and completing the corrective action plan.']
  responsible_officer_name varchar [note: 'Name of the executive or officer accountable for ensuring the corrective action plan is completed and compliance is restored.']
  revised_completion_date date [note: 'Updated target completion date following approval of an extension or plan modification by the regulatory authority.']
  root_cause_analysis_completed_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a formal root cause analysis was conducted to identify the underlying systemic issues that led to the violation.']
  root_cause_summary varchar [note: 'Summary of the root cause analysis findings identifying the fundamental reasons for the non-compliance or deficiency.']
  severity_level varchar [note: 'Severity classification of the underlying violation or finding as determined by the regulatory authority or internal risk assessment.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date on which the corrective action plan was formally submitted to the regulatory authority or internal compliance office for review.']
  target_completion_date date [note: 'Planned or mandated date by which all corrective actions must be completed and compliance fully restored.']
  verification_date date [note: 'Date on which the corrective actions were verified as complete and effective by the designated verification authority.']
  verification_method varchar [note: 'The method or process used to verify completion and effectiveness of corrective actions (e.g., internal audit, third-party assessment, regulatory inspection, self-certification).']
  verification_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the verification process indicating whether corrective actions have been validated as effective.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for corrective_action_plan. Referenced by corrective_action_plan_id.'
}

  violation_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique violation tracking number assigned by the utility or regulatory body.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for violation. Referenced by violation_id.'

  open_item_management boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this GL account uses open item management in SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud, meaning individual line items remain open until cleared by a matching offsetting entry. Typically enabled for clearing accounts, bank accounts, and GR/IR (Goods Receipt/Invoice Receipt) accounts. Supports accounts receivable and accounts payable reconciliation.']
  parent_account_number varchar [note: 'The account number of the parent/summary GL account in the chart-of-accounts hierarchy. Enables roll-up of detailed accounts into summary accounts for financial statement presentation and FERC Form 1/2 schedule aggregation. Null for top-level summary accounts.']
  plant_account_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this GL account is a utility plant account subject to FERC plant-in-service reporting, depreciation schedules, and rate base inclusion. True for accounts in the FERC 100-series (Electric Plant) and 200-series (Gas Plant). Used to filter accounts for AFUDC capitalization and depreciation rate studies.']
  posting_allowed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether direct journal entry postings are permitted to this GL account. False for summary/group accounts that only aggregate child accounts and do not accept direct postings. Sourced from the SAP S/4HANA account master \'Post Automatically Only\' or Oracle ERP Cloud \'Allow Posting\' flag.']
  rate_base_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether balances in this GL account are eligible for inclusion in the utility\'s rate base for rate case cost-of-service studies filed with FERC or state PUCs. Rate base typically includes net utility plant in service, working capital allowances, and regulatory assets. Used in PBR and traditional cost-of-service rate case models.']
  reconciliation_account_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this GL account is a reconciliation account (subledger control account) in SAP S/4HANA, meaning postings are made automatically from subledger modules (Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Asset Accounting) and direct manual postings are restricted. Critical for SOX subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation controls.']
  regulatory_asset_liability_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this GL account represents a regulatory asset or regulatory liability recognized under GAAP ASC 980 (Regulated Operations). Regulatory assets/liabilities arise from rate-regulated accounting deferrals approved by FERC or state PUCs (e.g., deferred fuel costs, storm damage deferrals, pension regulatory assets).']
  source_system_account_code varchar [note: 'The native account identifier as stored in the originating ERP system (SAP S/4HANA GL account number or Oracle ERP Cloud natural account segment value). Enables traceability from the Databricks Silver Layer record back to the source system for reconciliation and audit purposes.']
  sox_relevant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this GL account is within scope for Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) Section 404 internal controls over financial reporting. SOX-relevant accounts require documented controls, periodic testing, and management certification. Sourced from the SOX scoping assessment maintained by the internal audit and finance compliance teams.']
  tax_category varchar [note: 'The tax relevance category for this GL account in the ERP system, indicating whether the account is subject to sales/use tax, gross receipts tax, or is tax-exempt. Used in automated tax determination during invoice processing and in state PUC gross receipts tax reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: taxable_input|taxable_output|exempt|not_relevant — promote to reference product]']
  utility_function varchar [note: 'Identifies whether the GL account is associated with the electric utility function, gas utility function, common/shared services, or other non-utility operations. Critical for cost-of-service studies in rate cases, FERC Form 1 (electric) vs. FERC Form 2 (gas) filing segregation, and state PUC jurisdictional separation of revenues and expenses.']
  wip_account_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this GL account is a Work in Progress (WIP) / Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) account (FERC Account 107 – Construction Work in Progress – Electric, or equivalent gas account). WIP accounts accumulate capital project costs before transfer to plant-in-service upon project completion. Used in AFUDC calculation and capital project tracking.']

  Note: 'General ledger account master aligned to the FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USoA) chart of accounts for regulated electric and gas utilities. Captures account number, account name, FERC account code (e.g., Account 101 – Electric Plant in Service, Account 303 – Miscellaneous Intangible Plant), account type (asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense), normal balance indicator, and GAAP classification. Serves as the SSOT for all ledger postings, rate case cost-of-service studies, and FERC Form 1/2 regulatory filings. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud chart of accounts module.'

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overhead_lines|underground_cable|transformers|meters|gas_mains|buildings|it_equipment|generation_equipment|substation_equipment|vehicles — promote to reference product]']

  wbs_element varchar [note: 'The Work Breakdown Structure element code from SAP Project System (PS) or Oracle ERP Project module, used to track CAPEX budgets at the project or sub-project level.   Note: 'Annual and multi-year financial budget record for the utility, organized by cost center, GL account, functional area, and fiscal period. Captures budget version (original, revised, forecast, long-range plan), budget type (OPEX/O&M, CAPEX, revenue), fiscal year, period-level budget amounts, total approved budget amount, variance threshold percentage, budget owner, and approval status. Each budget record represents a unique combination of version, type, cost center, and GL account for a fiscal year. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO-PA) or Oracle ERP Cloud Budgetary Control module.'

  acquisition_date date [note: 'Date on which the utility acquired ownership or control of the asset (purchase date, transfer date, or contribution date).   asset_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the fixed asset in the utility plant subledger. \'in_service\' indicates the asset is placed in service and included in rate base. \'cwip\' indicates Construction Work in Progress not yet transferred to plant in service. \'retired\' indicates the asset has been removed from service.   asset_type varchar [note: 'Broad classification of the asset as tangible utility plant, intangible plant, or Construction Work in Progress (CWIP). Tangible includes physical generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure. Intangible includes software, licenses, and franchise rights. CWIP represents assets not yet placed in service.']
  capex_category varchar [note: 'Strategic CAPEX category classifying the business driver for the capital investment in this asset. \'growth\' supports customer or load growth. \'reliability\' improves grid or system reliability (SAIDI/SAIFI improvement). \'compliance\' meets regulatory or environmental mandates. \'replacement\' replaces end-of-life infrastructure. \'technology\' supports grid modernization or AMI deployment. Used in IRP and regulatory filings.']
  capitalization_threshold decimal(18,2) [note: 'Minimum dollar threshold applied to determine whether an expenditure on this asset class is capitalized as plant in service or expensed as O&M. Established by the utility\'s capitalization policy, approved by the board, and subject to SOX internal controls. Denominated in USD.']
  ciac_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount of Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) received from customers, developers, or third parties that offset the original cost of this asset. CIAC reduces the rate base for regulatory purposes. Tracked per FERC Account 271 and applicable state PUC tariff rules. Denominated in USD.']
  cost_of_removal decimal(18,2) [note: 'Actual or estimated cost incurred to remove the asset from service upon retirement (excavation, demolition, environmental remediation, disposal). Subtracted from gross salvage to determine net salvage. Frequently exceeds gross salvage for underground utility infrastructure, resulting in negative net salvage. Denominated in USD.']
  cwip_transfer_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier of the Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) work order or project from which this asset was transferred upon completion and placement in service. Links the capitalized plant record back to the capital project that funded its construction. Corresponds to FERC Account 107 (Construction Work in Progress) transfer transactions.']
  depreciation_group_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the depreciation group or composite account to which this asset belongs for group/composite depreciation purposes. Assets within the same depreciation group share a common composite depreciation rate derived from the FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Critical for utility industry group depreciation accounting.']
  depreciation_method varchar [note: 'Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation expense for this asset. \'straight_line\' allocates cost evenly over useful life. \'group_composite\' is the predominant utility industry method where assets are depreciated as a group using composite rates derived from depreciation studies approved by FERC or state PUCs. \'units_of_production\' is used for generation assets tied to output.']
  depreciation_study_year varchar [note: 'The year of the most recent FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study from which the depreciation rates, useful life, and net salvage rate for this asset class were derived. Depreciation studies are typically conducted every 3–5 years and filed with the applicable regulatory authority. Tracks which study vintage governs the current depreciation parameters.']
  ferc_plant_account varchar [note: 'FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account code to which this asset is classified (e.g., 101 Electric Plant in Service, 303 Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, 350 Land and Land Rights — Transmission, 376 Distribution Mains — Gas). Drives FERC Form 1 plant schedule reporting (Schedules 204–207) and rate base calculations.']
  ferc_plant_account_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive name corresponding to the FERC plant account code (e.g., \'Electric Plant in Service\', \'Distribution Mains — Gas\'). Supports human-readable reporting on FERC Form 1 plant schedules without requiring a join to a reference table.']
  functional_class varchar [note: 'FERC functional classification of the utility plant asset: Generation, Transmission, Distribution, General Plant, or Intangible. Drives allocation of rate base and O&M costs across customer classes in rate case cost-of-service studies.']
  gross_salvage_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Actual or estimated gross salvage proceeds received or expected upon retirement of the asset (scrap value, resale proceeds). Used in conjunction with cost of removal to compute net salvage for depreciation study updates. Populated upon retirement; null for in-service assets. Denominated in USD.']
  in_service_date date [note: 'Date on which the asset was placed in service and began depreciating. Triggers the start of depreciation accrual and inclusion in the utility rate base. For CWIP-to-plant transfers, this is the date the CWIP balance is transferred to plant in service. Critical for AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) cessation.']
  is_rate_base_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this asset is eligible for inclusion in the utility\'s regulatory rate base for cost-of-service rate case purposes. Assets funded by CIAC, regulatory disallowances, or held for future use may be excluded from rate base. Critical for PUC and FERC rate case filings.']
  is_regulatory_asset boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this item is classified as a regulatory asset under GAAP ASC 980 (Regulated Operations), meaning its recovery through future rates is probable. Regulatory assets arise from costs deferred for rate recovery (e.g., storm damage costs, deferred fuel costs, environmental remediation). Affects balance sheet presentation and rate case strategy.']
  last_physical_inventory_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent physical inventory verification confirming the existence and condition of this asset. Physical inventories are required for SOX compliance (internal controls over financial reporting) and support reconciliation between the fixed asset subledger and the operational asset register in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.']
  location_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the physical or operational location of the asset within the utility\'s service territory (e.g., substation identifier, distribution circuit code, gas pressure zone, plant site code). Used for geographic cost allocation in rate cases and for reconciliation with the GIS (ESRI ArcGIS) asset network model.']
  net_book_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Current net book value of the asset, calculated as original cost minus accumulated depreciation. Represents the carrying value of the asset on the utility\'s balance sheet and is the primary basis for rate base inclusion in cost-of-service rate cases. Denominated in USD. Note: while derivable, this field is stored for performance and regulatory reporting efficiency.']
  net_salvage_rate decimal(8,6) [note: 'The net salvage rate applied to this asset class in the depreciation study, expressed as a decimal. Net salvage equals gross salvage proceeds minus cost of removal. For utility assets, net salvage is frequently negative (negative salvage) because cost of removal (e.g., pole removal, underground cable excavation, gas main abandonment) exceeds any scrap value. Negative salvage rates increase the depreciable base and are a critical input unique to utility depreciation studies.']
  original_cost decimal(18,2) [note: 'The original cost of the utility plant asset at the time it was first dedicated to public service, as defined by FERC Uniform System of Accounts. Includes all costs necessary to bring the asset to its intended use (materials, labor, AFUDC, overhead). This is the FERC-defined original cost, not necessarily the acquisition cost paid by the current owner. Denominated in USD.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this fixed asset record was first created in the financial subledger system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Supports SOX audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this fixed asset record was most recently modified in the financial subledger system. Tracks changes to depreciation parameters, status updates, retirement entries, and cost adjustments. Supports SOX audit trail and Silver Layer change data capture (CDC) processing.']
  remaining_useful_life_years decimal(6,2) [note: 'Estimated remaining useful service life of the asset in years as of the most recent depreciation study or valuation date.   retirement_date date [note: 'Date on which the asset was retired, abandoned, or removed from utility plant in service. Triggers cessation of depreciation accrual and removal from rate base. Null for assets currently in service. Required for FERC Form 1 plant retirement schedules.']
  retirement_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the asset retirement event. \'normal\' retirements are expected end-of-life removals consistent with the depreciation study survivor curve. \'abnormal\' retirements are premature removals due to accidents, storms, or regulatory mandates. \'extraordinary\' retirements involve large-scale plant abandonments.   service_territory varchar [note: 'Name or code of the regulatory service territory or jurisdiction in which the asset is located (e.g., state name, PUC jurisdiction code). Determines which state Public Utility Commission (PUC) has regulatory jurisdiction over the asset\'s rate base treatment and depreciation rates.']
  useful_life_years decimal(6,2) [note: 'Estimated useful service life of the asset in years, as established in the most recent FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Used to compute straight-line depreciation rates and to project future capital replacement needs in the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). Decimal precision accommodates fractional lives from group/composite depreciation studies.']
  utility_type varchar [note: 'Identifies whether the asset belongs to the electric utility plant, gas utility plant, common plant (shared between electric and gas), or other. Critical for cost-of-service allocation studies in rate cases filed with state PUCs and FERC.']
  vintage_year varchar [note: 'The year in which the asset was originally constructed or manufactured. Critical input for group/composite depreciation studies unique to the utility industry, where survivor curve analysis and Iowa Curve fitting require age distribution data by vintage year. Used in FERC-approved depreciation studies and PUC rate case filings.']
  wbs_element varchar [note: 'Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element or capital project code from the ERP system associated with the construction or acquisition of this asset. Links the capitalized asset to the CAPEX project that funded it, supporting capital budget tracking and AFUDC calculation. Relevant for assets still in CWIP or recently transferred to plant in service.']

  Note: 'Master record for capitalized utility plant assets tracked in the fixed asset subledger, aligned to FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant accounts. Captures asset number, asset description, FERC plant account (e.g., 101 Electric Plant in Service, 303 Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, 376 Distribution Mains — Gas), asset class, vintage year, acquisition date, in-service date, original cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value, depreciation method (straight-line, group/composite), useful life, net salvage rate (including negative salvage/cost of removal), retirement date, retirement type (normal, abnormal, extraordinary), asset location, and CWIP-to-plant transfer reference. Serves as the financial SSOT for utility plant valuation, depreciation studies, rate base calculations, and FERC Form 1 plant schedules (Schedules 204-207). Complements the operational asset record in the asset domain. Vintage year and net salvage rate are critical for group/composite depreciation studies unique to the utility industry.'
}

  financial_period_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: depreciation_run has fiscal_year and fiscal_period attributes. financial_period is the master for fiscal periods. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full period metadata (period dates, s']
  gl_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: depreciation_run has gl_account_code attribute. gl_account is the master for GL accounts. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full account details (account_name, ferc_account_description,']
  accumulated_depreciation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total accumulated depreciation balance (in USD) for the assets processed in this run as of the end of the fiscal period, across the specified depreciation area. Represents the cumulative depreciation charged against the gross plant-in-service balance. Used in FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 and rate base calculations for rate cases.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the depreciation run was approved for posting by the authorized finance approver. Part of the SOX audit trail for the depreciation posting lifecycle.']

  asset_class_code varchar [note: 'FERC or ERP asset class code identifying the category of fixed assets included in this depreciation run (e.g., \'301\' = Organization, \'303\' = Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, \'350\' = Land and Land Rights, \'353\' = Station Equipment, \'362\' = Meters, \'391\' = Office Furniture). Aligns with FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account codes. If the run covers all asset classes, this field is null.']
  assets_errored_count varchar [note: 'Number of fixed asset records that encountered errors and were excluded from depreciation calculation during this run. A non-zero value requires investigation and potential rerun. Supports SOX completeness controls over the depreciation process.']
  assets_processed_count varchar [note: 'Total number of fixed asset records processed during this depreciation run. Used for run completeness validation, reconciliation against the fixed asset register count, and identifying partial runs or processing errors.']
  company_code varchar [note: 'SAP company code or ERP legal entity identifier representing the regulated utility entity (e.g., electric operating company, gas distribution company) for which the depreciation run was executed. Supports multi-entity utility holding company structures and separate FERC/PUC regulatory reporting by legal entity.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this depreciation run record was first captured in the data platform. Used for audit trail and SOX compliance over the depreciation posting process.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the depreciation amounts in this run (e.g., \'USD\'). Supports multi-currency reporting for utility holding companies with international operations.']
  depreciation_area_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the depreciation valuation area for which this run was executed. Common utility depreciation areas: \'01\' = Book/GAAP, \'10\' = Federal Tax (MACRS), \'15\' = State Tax, \'20\' = Regulatory/FERC, \'30\' = Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT), \'40\' = Group/Composite. Each area maintains independent depreciation values per SAP FI-AA configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 01|10|15|20|30|40 — promote to reference product]']
  depreciation_area_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the depreciation area (e.g., \'Book/GAAP\', \'Federal Tax MACRS\', \'State Tax\', \'Regulatory/FERC\', \'Alternative Minimum Tax\', \'Group/Composite\'). Supports reporting and audit trail readability without requiring a join to a reference table.']
  depreciation_method_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the depreciation calculation method applied during this run. \'SL\' = Straight-Line (primary GAAP method for utilities); \'GRP\' = Group/Composite (common for utility plant accounts per FERC); \'SYD\' = Sum-of-Years-Digits; \'DB\' = Declining Balance; \'UOP\' = Units-of-Production. Determines the mathematical basis for depreciation expense calculation.']
  depreciation_method_name varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the depreciation method applied (e.g., \'Straight-Line\', \'Group/Composite\', \'Sum-of-Years-Digits\', \'Declining Balance\', \'Units-of-Production\'). Supports FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 reporting and rate case cost-of-service documentation.']
  depreciation_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'The composite or average depreciation rate (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.033333 for 3.3333%) applied during this run. For group/composite depreciation, this is the PUC-approved composite rate from the most recent depreciation study. For straight-line, this is the reciprocal of the average service life. Key parameter for depreciation study true-up analysis.']
  depreciation_rate_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the depreciation rates applied in this run are interim rates (provisionally approved by the PUC pending final order), final rates (approved in a final PUC order), proposed rates (filed but not yet approved), or approved rates (in effect under current tariff). Critical for regulatory accounting and rate case true-up calculations.']
  error_message varchar [note: 'System-generated error message text when run_status = \'error\'. Captures the ERP error description to support troubleshooting and resolution of failed depreciation runs. Null when the run completed successfully.']
  ferc_plant_account varchar [note: 'FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account number to which the depreciation expense from this run is attributed (e.g., \'403\' = Depreciation Expense — Electric, \'404\' = Amortization of Limited-Term Electric Plant). Required for FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 depreciation and amortization reporting.']
  fiscal_period varchar [note: 'The accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year to which this depreciation run applies. Determines the general ledger period into which depreciation expense is posted.']
  fiscal_year varchar [note: 'The fiscal year (four-digit integer, e.g., 2024) to which this depreciation run applies. Aligns with the utility\'s GAAP and FERC regulatory accounting fiscal year for financial statement preparation and FERC Form 1 reporting.']
  gross_plant_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total gross plant-in-service value (in USD) of the assets processed in this depreciation run as of the run date. Represents the depreciable asset base. Used to validate the depreciation rate applied (total_depreciation_amount / gross_plant_amount) and supports rate base calculations in rate case cost-of-service studies.']
  is_repeat_run boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this run is a repeat execution for a period that was previously processed (True) or a first-time run for the period (False). Repeat runs occur after reversals or corrections. Relevant for SOX controls over duplicate depreciation postings.']
  is_simulation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this depreciation run was executed in simulation (test) mode without posting to the general ledger (True) or as a live posting run (False). Simulation runs are used to preview depreciation amounts before period-end close.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes entered by the run initiator or approver describing the purpose, scope, or any exceptions associated with this depreciation run (e.g., \'Year-end true-up run applying final PUC-approved rates from Docket 2024-001\', \'Repeat run after reversal of period 6 posting error\').']
  planned_depreciation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The budgeted or planned depreciation amount for this fiscal period and depreciation area, as established in the depreciation study or annual budget. Compared against total_depreciation_amount to identify variances for depreciation study true-up analysis and rate case cost-of-service reconciliation.']
  posting_date date [note: 'The date on which the depreciation amounts were posted to the general ledger. May differ from run_date if the run was simulated first and posted later. Critical for period-end close cutoff and GAAP accrual accounting.']
  posting_document_number varchar [note: 'ERP financial document number (e.g., SAP FI document number) generated when depreciation amounts are posted to the general ledger. Provides the audit trail linkage between the depreciation run and the actual GL posting for SOX compliance and external audit support.']
  reversal_date date [note: 'The date on which the depreciation run posting was reversed in the general ledger. Null if not reversed. Used in conjunction with reversal_document_number to track corrected depreciation entries.']
  reversal_document_number varchar [note: 'ERP financial document number of the reversal posting if this depreciation run was reversed. Null if the run has not been reversed. Supports audit trail for corrected depreciation postings and SOX compliance.']
  run_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the depreciation calculation run was executed. This is the principal business event date — the date the depreciation program was triggered in the asset accounting system.']
  run_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the depreciation calculation program completed execution. Used with run_start_timestamp to measure total processing duration for operational monitoring of the period-end close process.']
  run_initiator varchar [note: 'User ID or system account that initiated the depreciation run in the ERP system. Required for SOX audit trail to establish accountability over the depreciation posting process and segregation of duties compliance.']
  run_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier assigned to the depreciation run by the ERP system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA depreciation run document number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail reference.']
  run_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the depreciation calculation program began execution in the ERP system. Used with run_end_timestamp to measure processing duration and identify performance issues with large asset portfolios.']
  run_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the depreciation run. \'planned\' indicates scheduled but not yet executed; \'simulated\' indicates a test run without posting; \'posted\' indicates amounts have been committed to the general ledger; \'reversed\' indicates the posting has been reversed; \'error\' indicates the run failed during processing.']
  run_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the depreciation run by its business purpose. \'periodic\' = standard monthly/quarterly run; \'year_end\' = annual closing run; \'special\' = off-cycle run for asset disposals or acquisitions; \'repeat\' = rerun of a previously executed period.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this depreciation run record was sourced (e.g., \'SAP_S4\', \'ORACLE_ERP\'). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.']
  total_depreciation_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total depreciation expense amount (in USD) calculated and posted during this run across all assets processed. This is the gross depreciation charge for the period and depreciation area. Key input for rate case cost-of-service calculations, FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 reporting, and GAAP income statement depreciation expense line.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this depreciation run record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks status changes such as reversal or error correction for SOX audit trail.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of periodic depreciation calculation runs executed against the fixed asset subledger. Captures run date, fiscal period, fiscal year, depreciation area (book/GAAP, federal tax, state tax, regulatory/FERC, AMT, group/composite), total depreciation amount posted, number of assets processed, run status (planned, simulated, posted, reversed), posting document reference, run initiator, and depreciation method applied (straight-line, group/composite, sum-of-years-digits, declining balance, units-of-production). Supports GAAP straight-line and group/composite depreciation methods commonly used by utilities, regulatory depreciation per PUC-approved depreciation study rates (including interim and final rates), tax depreciation (MACRS with bonus depreciation), and FERC Form 1 depreciation reporting (Schedule 336 — Depreciation and Amortization of Electric Plant). Enables audit trail for SOX compliance over the depreciation posting process, supports depreciation study true-up analysis, and provides the depreciation expense input for rate case cost-of-service calculations.'
}
